entities.name: Rodrigo de Sousa Coutinho
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rodrigo de Sousa Coutinho, 1st Count of Linhares was a Portuguese nobleman and politician who played a crucial role in the Portuguese Restoration War (1792-1802) and the Napoleonic Wars (1803-1815).

As a member of the Junta Central, he contributed to the establishment of the Portuguese Junta, a governing body that aimed to restore the Portuguese monarchy.

Coutinho's leadership during the Battle of Vimeiro (1792) and the Siege of Lisbon (1808) was instrumental in securing key victories for the Portuguese forces.

The Count's legacy extends beyond his military victories, as he helped shape the modern Portuguese state and its institutions.

A striking testament to his enduring impact is the Linhares Palace, a stunning example of Portuguese Baroque architecture that still stands today.

Rodrigo de Sousa Coutinho's life serves as a testament to the complex and multifaceted nature of 19th-century European history.
